subject.title: bug(telegram): reply to bot photo injects bot-sent media as inbound user attachment

question: Should a reply to an OpenClaw-authored Telegram media message retain that media for model context, or should self-authored reply-target media be excluded while text and reply metadata remain visible?
rationale: Current main intentionally hydrates reply-chain media broadly, while this report identifies that the same mechanism can make bot-generated media appear as a new inbound attachment. Source inspection cannot choose the desired user-facing context contract.

options.title: Exclude self-authored reply media
options.body: Keep reply-chain text and sender metadata, but skip attachment hydration when the reply target is authored by the configured bot.

options.title: Retain current hydration
options.body: Keep bot-authored reply-target media available to the model and document that a reply can reintroduce the referenced media as context.

recommendation.title: Exclude self-authored reply media
recommendation.body: Keep reply-chain text and sender metadata, but skip attachment hydration when the reply target is authored by the configured bot.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged reply-chain media work is the clearest current-main provenance for the overlapping behavior.
